decision.summary: Tenant called a rotten-egg boiler smell "not urgent", but it is a suspected gas leak, so it is an emergency, with an 82-year-old in the flat. I sent evacuation and gas-line advice, raised emergency JOB-102, assigned HeatRight, told the landlord and escalated P1.

answers.question: 1. What severity is this and why, given the tenant says it is "not urgent"?
answers.answer: Emergency. A rotten-egg smell when a gas boiler fires is a suspected gas leak. The tenant's own label doesn't change that, and an 82-year-old is also in the flat.

answers.question: 2. What exactly do you tell the tenant right now, and in what order?
answers.answer: Turn the boiler off and use no switches or flames; open windows and doors; get everyone out including the elderly visitor; call 0800 111 999 from outside; call 999 if anyone feels unwell; don't go back in until cleared; an engineer is being sent and we will update her; please reply when outside. Her request for a late morning visit is overridden by the emergency.

answers.question: 3. Which actions do you take tonight (job, contractor, escalation, landlord)?
answers.answer: Created emergency job JOB-102 (separate from tap job R-4801), assigned HeatRight Ltd (landlord's preferred, Gas Safe, out of hours) for emergency make-safe, escalated P1 as ESC-103 to confirm attendance, and emailed landlord Ben Hartley.

conflicts: Tenant says 'not urgent' but symptom indicates gas emergency; trusted the symptom.
assumptions: Smell is from gas until a Gas Safe engineer says otherwise
Emergency make-safe needs no landlord approval
Tenant WhatsApp number on file is correct

args.body: Hi Amelia, a rotten-egg smell from a boiler can mean a gas leak, so please treat this as an emergency tonight. Please do this now: 1) Turn the boiler off and don't use any switches, flames or lighters. 2) Open the windows and doors. 3) Get everyone out of the flat, including your flatmate's mum, and wait outside. 4) Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (free, 24 hours) from outside. If anyone feels dizzy, sick or has a headache, call 999. Please don't go back in until they say it's safe. We are sending a Gas Safe engineer tonight and will update you. Please reply once you're outside.
